methodology.title: 2.1 Core Principle: Science CLIL Integration
content: Problem: Students know the word "butterfly" or "frog" but cannot scientifically describe how animals grow and change over time.

Solution: We explicitly teach the stages of metamorphosis (egg, larva, pupa, adult) integrated with sequence words (First, Next, Then, Finally) and present simple verbs. This allows students to logically describe biological processes step by step.

methodology.title: 2.2 Session Flow (120 Minutes)
content: Session 1: Introduce the 4 stages of a butterfly's life cycle. Focus on connecting sequence words with the new Tier 1 vocabulary.
Session 2: Explore the life cycle of an amphibian (frog). Compare the stages and practice describing continuous changes in nature.
Session 3: Full production. Write a cohesive scientific report explaining an animal's life cycle from birth to adult, and present it orally.

methodology.title: 2.4 Teacher Notes: Pull-Out Tasks & Communicative Task
content: S1 pull-out: Show a picture of one life stage (e.g., a pupa). The student must name it and sequence it ("This is the pupa. It is the third stage.").

Communicative task (Step 5 - 10 min): The Cycle Builder. Student A has the pictures out of order. Student B reads the steps using "First, Next...". Student A must arrange the pictures correctly based on the listening.

vocab_tiers.Memory Trick: TAD + POLE = a tad (little bit) of a pole (stick) → a tiny stick with a head!

vocab_tiers.Key Collocation(s): the sequence of stages / in correct sequence

vocab_tiers.Key Collocation(s): first, the egg hatches / first stage

vocab_tiers.Key Collocation(s): then it grows / then the larva forms

vocab_tiers.Key Collocation(s): next, it becomes a pupa / the next stage

content: 📖 From Egg to Adult
The butterfly has 4 stages.
First, eggs ARE LAID on leaves by the female butterfly.
Then, the eggs HATCH and a larva (caterpillar) IS BORN.
The caterpillar EATS leaves and grows.
Next, a chrysalis IS FORMED around the caterpillar.
Inside the chrysalis, wings ARE DEVELOPED.
Finally, a beautiful butterfly IS RELEASED.
The frog also has 4 stages: eggs -> tadpole -> froglet -> adult frog.
The mosquito is the most dangerous insect: it IS CLASSIFIED as a disease carrier.
Welcome to my science presentation! I am Detective Max.
Today, I will compare the amazing life cycles of a butterfly and a frog.
Both animals change their bodies a lot.
First, both the butterfly and the frog lay eggs. This is the first stage.
Next, a larva hatches. The butterfly larva is a hungry worm. The frog larva is a swimming tadpole.
Then, they change in different ways. Unlike the frog, the butterfly has a pupa stage. It rests inside a hard shell. The frog does not have a pupa. It grows legs in the water.
Finally, both animals become adults. The adult butterfly flies in the sky. The adult frog jumps on the land.
Life cycles are wonderful to observe! Thank you for listening!

listening_script.text: Hello, biologists! Today we are studying the life cycle of a butterfly. A life cycle has four stages. First, a butterfly lays a tiny egg on a leaf. Next, the egg hatches into a larva — we call it a caterpillar. Then, the caterpillar becomes a pupa inside a chrysalis. Finally, the pupa transforms into a beautiful adult butterfly. The cycle then begins again when the butterfly lays new eggs. Listen and number the stages in the correct order on your worksheet!

SPEAKING CHECKPOINT — Teacher Guidance (do NOT share with students):

Student A: Ask "What happens first?"
Student B: Answer "First, the butterfly lays an egg."
Goal: Practice sequence words with life stages.
[O] L3 — Fill in the blank with 3 options (10 items)
The butterfly has a life _______________ (cycle / desert / adult).
The _______________ (adult / stage / egg) is the first part of the cycle.
First, the mother butterfly _______________ (lays / hatches / gives) an egg.
Next, a hungry _______________ (pupa / larva / adult) comes out.
The larva eats leaves to _______________ (grow / sleep / fly) big.
Then, it changes into a hard _______________ (pupa / egg / larva).
Inside the pupa, the insect is _______________ (dangerous / safe / wet).
Finally, an _______________ (adult / egg / stage) butterfly appears.
The adult _______________ (uses / making / eats) its wings to fly.
There are four _______________ (stages / cycles / adults) in total.
[O] L4 — Sentence Expansion (Sequencing) (10 items)
Base: The butterfly lays an egg. + Add: (First,) → ________________________________________

listening_script.text: Good morning! I will now present my life cycle report for the class. I chose the mosquito because it has a very clear four-stage cycle. First, the adult mosquito lays eggs on the surface of water. Next, the eggs hatch into larvae that wiggle and swim in the water. Then, the larvae become pupae and stop eating while they change.
